text:
marta: Heads up: found a suspicious object in partner-logs S3 that looks like a wrapped KMS blob containing Vault transit ciphertext. Path: s3://partner-logs/ingest/2026-03-20/backup-20260320.blob

ben: Can you paste the object key + size + sha256?

marta: backup-20260320.blob (4.1 MB) sha256: 9f2c4e1a... (truncated)

marta: Header starts with "KMSv1" which matches our KMS-wrap format. Might be transit-wrapped, not raw KV.

samir: Good catch. Immediate: 1) remove partner ingest SA from KMS decrypt grants; 2) snapshot and isolate object for forensics; 3) create incident ticket. Infra, can you revoke key binding?

infra-oncall: Running: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/ingest-key --member=serviceAccount:partner-ingest@partner.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter`

infra-oncall: IAM binding removed. Copied blob to gs://redwood-forensics/2794412345/backup-20260320.blob

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-045 created (priority: P2) 023-03-20T14:12Z 026 assigned to eng-security.

jess: Assume worst: partner blob could allow rewrap/unseal if transit key used. Plan: rotate Vault transit key, rewrap affected ciphertexts, revoke old key. Samir can you coordinate with Vault ops?

samir: Steps: create new transit key (transit/new-ingest-2026-03-20), dry-run rewrap of secret/ingest/*, canary rewrap one consumer, bulk rewrap, back up old ciphertexts.

marta: Partner says it was accidental upload and will cooperate; SA was used earlier this month.

ben: Scope blast radius: which systems use that KMS key? Any long-lived tokens with decrypt perms?

infra-oncall: Audit: key had bindings to partner-ingest SA and backup-archiver SA only. No human IAMs; no compute attachments. Binding removed.

samir: Creating new transit key: `vault write -f transit/keys/new-ingest-2026-03-20`

samir: Dry-run list shows 27 ciphertexts under secret/ingest referencing old key. Will canary rewrap ingest-worker config.

jess: Coordinate with product owners to avoid breaking live jobs.

samir: Canary rewrap succeeded for ingest-worker. Proceeding: `vault write transit/rewrap ciphertext=@cipherlist.json to_key=new-ingest-2026-03-20`

infra-oncall: Bulk rewrap complete. 27 items rewrapped. Saved old ciphertexts to gs://redwood-forensics/2794412345/old-ciphertexts/

jess: Next: create a new KMS key version and disable old versions, update cloud-kms-seal config, roll Vault nodes.

marta: Forensics: sent header sample to legal for TLP guidance. Partner provided signed attestation they deleted the accidental backup and rotated ingestion tokens.

ben: Action items recap: infra removed IAM binding (done); samir created new transit key + rewrapped vault ciphertexts (done); jess to rotate KMS versions + update configs (in progress); marta to coordinate partner attestation + legal (in progress).

jess: KMS new version created: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/partner/cryptoKeys/ingest-key/cryptoKeyVersions/3. Disabled old version 2. Rolling deploy of cloud-kms-seal to Vault nodes starting now (one node at a time).

infra-oncall: vault-seal-updater roll started; rolling restart of 3 nodes.

security-bot: INC-2026-045 updated: mitigations applied, monitoring enabled.

marta: Marking thread for postmortem. Add timeline to INC-2026-045 and owners for follow-ups: RBAC hardening, periodic key binding audit, partner onboarding checklist update.

ben: I'll own RBAC audit. Jess, can you own onboarding checklist update?

jess: Yep. Adding a required step to verify backups are not uploaded to partner buckets and require an allowlist for S3 destinations.

samir: I'll draft a runbook for rewraps and emergency key eviction and link it to the incident.

marta: Thanks all. Closing here, INC stays open for postmortem and follow-ups. :thumbsup:
